description: Composite figure: one large strain-hardening-rate curve with six circular microstructure schematics overlaid on it. Plot axes are y = "Stain hardening rate (MPa)" (0-5000) and x = "True strain" (0.0-0.6); legend identifies the thick dark-blue curve as "3Cr steel" and the light-blue curve as "2Ni steel". The 3Cr curve collapses from the top of the axis at zero strain to a sharp minimum at very low strain, rises to a peak just above the 2000 MPa gridline near true strain 0.2-0.25, then declines and drops to zero shortly before strain 0.4. The 2Ni curve dips to about the 1000 MPa gridline at low strain, peaks between the 1000 and 2000 MPa gridlines near strain 0.2, then falls to zero near strain 0.26. Six hexagonal-grain schematics, labelled (a) 3%, (b) 10%, (c) LD, (d) 5%, (e) 10%, (f) LD, depict the deformation microstructure of 3Cr steel (a-c) and 2Ni steel (d-f) at increasing strain; the bottom key defines HDDA, Slip band, Deformation twins and (partly cropped) stacking faults. Together the panels argue that 3Cr steel evolves through HDDA generation and progressively refined slip bands, whereas 2Ni steel deforms mainly by uniformly multiplying planar slip bands.

observations.observation: The plot y-axis is labelled 'Stain hardening rate (MPa)' with ticks 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, and the x-axis is 'True strain' spanning 0.0 to 0.6.
The legend names two curves: thick dark-blue = '3Cr steel' and light-blue = '2Ni steel'.
The 3Cr steel curve rises to a maximum just above the 2000 MPa gridline at true strain roughly 0.2-0.25 and falls to zero just before true strain 0.4; no numeric peak value is printed on the panel.

The 2Ni steel curve has an early minimum near the 1000 MPa gridline, a peak between the 1000 and 2000 MPa gridlines at about true strain 0.2, and reaches zero near true strain 0.26, i.e. lower and shorter than the 3Cr curve.
Six hexagonal-grain schematics are labelled (a) 3%, (b) 10%, (c) LD, (d) 5%, (e) 10%, (f) LD, with (a-c) placed over the left/upper region and (d-f) over the right/lower region of the plot.

A symbol key along the bottom of the figure defines HDDA (wavy line symbol), Slip band (dashed lines), Deformation twins (solid lines) and a fourth entry rendered as 'Stack fa...' whose full wording is cropped.
Panels (a) and (b) show sparse then denser parallel/crossing planar slip bands with HDDA symbols, while (c) shows the finest slip bands together with deformation twins and stacking faults.
Panels (d), (e) and (f) show slip bands that are relatively uniformly distributed and multiply with decreasing spacing as strain increases, with only occasional twin/stacking-fault markings.
The caption states the figure is a schematic diagram showing deformation microstructure at different strain stages in (a-c) 3Cr steel and (d-e) 2Ni steel.
The caption assigns only (d-e) to 2Ni steel, whereas the citing text repeatedly refers to 'Fig. 12d-f' for 2Ni steel and uses all three of d-f; the caption label appears to be a typo.

The citing text states that in 3Cr steel the initial plastic-deformation stage shows planar dislocation activity with dislocations constrained within planar slip bands, then stage II is characterised by appearance and proliferation of HDDA, and stage III by mutual annihilation, cross-slip and refinement of slip bands.
The citing text states that stacking faults and deformation twins occur in 3Cr steel only at very high strain levels near ultimate failure (Fig. 12c).

The citing text states that 2Ni steel deforms mainly by plane slip with relatively uniformly distributed slip bands that multiply and decrease in spacing with strain, and that a small number of stacking faults appear at very high strain close to final failure (Fig. 12e).
The citing text concludes that Cr alloying of Fe-Mn-Al-C steels promotes the DSBR and HDDA effects of plastic deformation and can increase elongation.

subfigures.description: Strain hardening rate (MPa, 0-5000) versus true strain (0.0-0.6). Dark-blue '3Cr steel' curve: sharp minimum at low strain, maximum just above 2000 MPa at strain ~0.2-0.25, then steep fall to zero just before 0.4. Light-blue '2Ni steel' curve: minimum near 1000 MPa, lower peak near strain 0.2, reaching zero near strain 0.26.
Schematic labelled '3%' (3Cr steel): hexagonal grain outlines containing sparse parallel planar slip bands and a few wavy HDDA symbols, i.e. the early planar-slip stage.
Schematic labelled '10%' (3Cr steel): denser, crossing slip bands with abundant wavy HDDA symbols inside several hexagons, indicating slip-band proliferation and HDDA activity.
Schematic labelled 'LD' (3Cr steel, large deformation): mostly filled with very fine, closely spaced slip bands plus solid-line deformation twins and dotted stacking-fault markings in the grains.
Schematic labelled '5%' (2Ni steel): hexagons with relatively uniformly distributed, moderately spaced slip bands and few HDDA marks.
Schematic labelled '10%' (2Ni steel): slip bands multiplied with reduced spacing between them; a small number of twin/stacking-fault markings appears.
Schematic labelled 'LD' (2Ni steel, large deformation): densely and uniformly banded grains with the smallest band spacing among the 2Ni panels.

unreadable_items: bottom symbol key: fourth entry is cropped, legible only as 'Stack fa...' (presumably stacking faults)
no numeric data labels are printed on either strain-hardening-rate curve; values can only be bracketed by gridlines
fine detail of individual symbols inside schematics (a)-(f) is small and partly illegible at the supplied resolution
